transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-16
Start: 11:29 AM UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (SE), Morgan (CSM), Ellen (MarrowBridge CTO), Marcus (Head of Platform), Renee (Security), Tom (PM)

Summary: Quick intro, architecture intake, compliance ask, perf bench plan, next steps and owners.

[00:00:12] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on — Alex from Redwood here, I'm the AE on this account. Appreciate you all making time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:23] Ellen: Hey Alex, Ellen Park here, CTO at MarrowBridge.
[00:00:25] Marcus: Marcus Diaz, Head of Platform.
[00:00:27] Renee: Renee Cho, security.
[00:00:30] Tom: Tom Alvarez, PM leading the integration.
[00:00:33] Alex: Great. Priya from SE and Morgan from Success are with me — Priya you want to intro?
[00:00:38] Priya: Hi all, Priya Narang, solutions engineer. I'll be your point for the initial benchmark and infra mapping, thanks.
[00:00:45] Morgan: Morgan Lee, CSM. I'll run the onboarding cadence and runbooks.

[00:01:10] Alex: Objective today is a short launch brief — confirm target timeline, pick deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and surface any blockers for security or network. We'll also agree next steps for a perf test. This should be quick, we have about 50-ish mins.

[00:02:05] Ellen: High level — we want Redwood because we need predictable latency for interactive features and lower token cost than our current in-house stack. Our timeline is Q3 pilot, production by mid Q4 ideally. Need to validate latency and costs before committing.

[00:02:45] Alex: Totally, that's consistent with other customers. Quick question on current stack — how are you serving models today?
[00:02:52] Marcus: We're self-hosted on k8s with mixed GPU fleet (A10s + older T4s). We do a weight based routing, but KV cache is pretty manual; our cache isn't great so cold-start latency spikes.
[00:03:15] Priya: Got it, that KV cache behavior is common — we have prefix caching and automatic KV management in the runtime. We might suggest a quantized variant for cost first pass.
[00:03:35] Marcus: One ask — we'd like a quantization demo; we heard Redwood can do int8 paths that shave cost without big perf regression.
[00:03:45] Priya: Yep, we'll show quant profiles in the bench. Note sometimes the nomenclature in docs reads Redwood Dedic vs Redwood Dedicated — sorry, voice auto picks it up funny.

[00:04:20] Tom: On stakeholders — security wants privacy review, infra needs network peering + IAM, product wants a short POC to validate UX. We're aiming to start the POC in three weeks.
[00:04:35] Alex: Sounds reasonable. For the POC we'd usually do a staging pool on Redwood Dedicated or Private if you need V P C. Any constraints on hosting?
[00:04:50] Renee: We need V P C peering or private deployment; default hosted API isn't acceptable for PHI. Also need SOC 2 type II docs, SAML S S O, and evidence of K M S integration or BYOK.
[00:05:05] Morgan: Noted. We'll pull together the security pack. Alex — do we have a standard compliance doc for this?
[00:05:12] Alex: Yes, we'll send the SOC docs and the K M S integration guide. We'll also include our audit logs spec — sometimes the auto transcription calls it audit logs but it's just JSON append-only logs with retention controls.

[00:05:45] Ellen: Also data residency — we need EU region for EU customer data. Is that covered?
[00:05:52] Alex: Yes, we have EU regions and Private/VPC options. For Dedicated, you can pin region. We'll include region notes in the checklist.

[00:06:20] Priya: Quick architecture question — Marcus, can you share network egress patterns? Do you have dedicated NAT, or do you expect direct peering?
[00:06:30] Marcus: We can do either but prefer direct peering to avoid egress cost surprises. We'll provide the CIDR ranges.
[00:06:40] Priya: Perfect. That makes the V P C setup straightforward.

[00:07:10] Alex: On perf — Priya, can you outline the benchmark plan?
[00:07:15] Priya: Sure. We'll run two tests: latency p50/p95 on a small prompt workload that mimics your UI flows, and throughput test on a larger batch for offline inference. We'll also test a quantized variant and a full fp16 variant. We'll collect token/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and cold-start distribution. Plan to run first bench on our staging pool using a model variant close to your target.
[00:07:48] Tom: How long does that take?
[00:07:50] Priya: The initial run takes a day to configure and an hour to run if we have sample payloads. Sharing sample dataset removes guesswork.
[00:08:02] Alex: Action: Priya will run bench if MarrowBridge shares sample payloads. Itemized in next steps.

[00:08:30] Ellen: A question on cost model — do Dedicated contracts have burst? We might overshoot during peak and need burst capacity.
[00:08:40] Alex: Yes, Dedicated plans include burst credits or burst pools as an add-on depending on your commit level. We'll send concrete SKUs.
[00:08:52] Marcus: Any SLA numbers for latency? We need to know expected SLOs for interactive routes.
[00:09:00] Alex: We publish latency medians per model; for Dedicated we offer latency-backed SLAs on throughput and availability. We'll share the latency profile docs.

[00:09:30] Renee: Security detail — on K M S, do you integrate with customer-managed keys? We need BYOK and hardware module support.
[00:09:40] Priya: Yes, BYOK with supported K M S providers; H S M integration is available for Private deployments. We'll attach the K M S guide and a note about key rotation.

[00:10:10] Tom: Regarding SAML — we run Okta, need provisioning via S C I M and groups mapped to RBAC.
[00:10:18] Morgan: We support SAML + SCIM; mapping to per-team role-based access is standard. We'll provide the SSO runbook.

[00:10:40] Alex: Quick intake on timeline: POC start target = 2026-05-07, two-week POC, then evaluation, aim for prod mid Q4. Any blockers to that?
[00:10:52] Ellen: Need the SOC docs and a clear cost estimate. If the POC shows latency and cost OK, we'll proceed.

[00:11:20] Priya: For the bench, Marcus — can you attach sample prompts and a set of 50 interactive flows? If you can give us an S3 link or share via secure dropbox that helps.
[00:11:32] Marcus: We'll prepare and send an S3 link by EOD on Monday.

[00:12:00] Priya: Great. One note — when we run the bench we sometimes see transcription weirdness in the auto tools where Kubernetes becomes 'cube-urn-ettes' — ignore that, it's the transcriber. We'll attach a clean PDF of logs.

[00:12:30] Tom: On observability — we want token-level cost breakdown per route and tracing for each request. Is that available out of the box?
[00:12:40] Alex: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdown, traces, and error analysis. You can also forward traces to your DataDog or New Relic. We'll include links to the console screenshots.

[00:13:15] Renee: For compliance, in addition to SOC2, we may need a pen test report and vulnerability scan. Is that something you can provide?
[00:13:25] Alex: We can provide third-party penetration test summaries and our internal vuln scanning cadence. Some details are redacted but we can provide attestations.

[00:13:55] Ellen: Is there a recommended architecture for on-prem? We might need an air-gapped option for a later stage.
[00:14:03] Priya: We support an on-prem package with a private control plane; it'll require an initial install window and some additional services. We can do a separate scoping call for air-gap specifics.

[00:14:28] Alex: Good. Let's capture immediate blockers: security docs, sample prompts, V P C peering ranges, and pricing SKUs. Anything else?
[00:14:40] Marcus: Network egress constraints — will need clarification on whether Redwood requires outbound to certain endpoints for model downloads or updates.
[00:14:50] Priya: Model artifacts can be mirrored; we have controlled image pulls and can support manifest-based sync for Private deployments. We'll document that.

[00:15:20] Tom: Ok, let's talk operational support — during POC who do we contact for urgent infra issues?
[00:15:27] Morgan: For POC we'll provide a priority support contact and Slack channel. If you pick a Dedicated plan, we can upgrade SLA access.

[00:16:00] Alex: Now a quick walkthrough of the proposed two-week POC cadence: week 0 — network and creds, week 1 — bench and smoke tests, week 2 — integration with your app and UX sign-off.
[00:16:18] Ellen: That seems fine. If we can start network on 04-20, bench by 04-23, that aligns.

[00:16:45] Priya: Regarding quantization — we'll test int8 and a middle ground 4bit hybrid to show cost/latency tradeoffs. Often quant helps with throughput at small latency cost.
[00:16:58] Marcus: Good. We'll want the exact model variants and epoch/perf deltas.

[00:17:30] Alex: Any concerns on data retention? Can you confirm retention window requirements?
[00:17:36] Renee: We need logs only for 90 days by default, but we need an option to purge on demand for certain datasets.
[00:17:44] Priya: We support configurable retention and immediate purge APIs for Private deployments; for Hosted we'll work with retention windows and SLA'd purge processes.

[00:18:10] Tom: A small nit — can you provide an example runbook for credential rotation and incident response?
[00:18:17] Morgan: Yes, we'll share a runbook template and an incident escalation path.

[00:18:45] Alex: Ok walking through immediate deliverables and owners — Priya: bench; Alex: pricing and contract; Morgan: schedule and runbooks; Renee: list of compliance docs you require. Sound right?
[00:18:58] Ellen: Yes. Also please include region selection notes for EU data.

[00:19:20] Priya: Small technical note — when doing latency tests, send prompts with realistic prefix lengths; sometimes customers test with unrealistically short prompts and that skews results.
[00:19:32] Marcus: We'll include a mix of 32–512 token flows.

[00:20:00] Priya: We'll also capture KV cache hit rates — if you can expose existing cache stats, that helps.
[00:20:10] Marcus: We'll export current cache metrics.

[00:21:00] Alex: Any legal procurement concerns we should know now?
[00:21:05] Tom: We'll need to route contract through our procurement team; payment terms probably net 45, but we can negotiate.
[00:21:12] Alex: Noted. We'll include standard terms and flag points for procurement.

[00:22:00] Ellen: One more question — do you support model version pinning so we don't get surprises on model updates?
[00:22:08] Priya: Absolutely — you can pin model revisions per-route and we have rollout/canary tooling to move traffic.

[00:22:40] Marcus: On monitoring, can we forward logs to our SIEM?
[00:22:45] Morgan: Yes, we support forwarding to common SIEMs; will include the endpoint formats.

[00:23:20] Alex: Alright let's have a brief demo snippet — Priya, can you show how we configure a Dedicated route and view token breakdown?
[00:23:28] Priya: (screen share) Here is the console — route config, model pin, batching policy, autoscale. Note the Console sometimes shows micro metrics as 'micrometrics' but the data is accurate.
[00:24:10] Priya: (walks through) This panel shows per-route token cost and p50/p95 latency. You can drill down by API key.
[00:24:45] Tom: That's helpful. Can we see an example of a fallback policy if Dedicated capacity runs out?
[00:24:52] Priya: Yes, you can set an automatic fallback to a compatible model in hosted region — we'll show compatibility matrix in the doc we send.

[00:25:20] Marcus: If we fall back, is there a difference in token accounting?
[00:25:24] Alex: The cost may differ by model variant and region; Console reports actual cost by token per call.

[00:26:00] Ellen: Ok, I want to confirm the bench outputs we'll get — raw logs, token counts, latency percentiles, and cost estimates.
[00:26:08] Priya: Yes, raw logs plus a summary deck and recommended config changes.

[00:26:40] Morgan: We'll send a schedule invite for weekly touchpoints. I suggest Tuesdays 10AM for the next four weeks — works for you?
[00:26:50] Ellen: Works for us.

[00:27:20] Alex: Any final concerns?
[00:27:28] Renee: Just to reiterate, SOC 2 plus BYOK details and any redactions noted. We may need a tighter NDA for some artifacts.
[00:27:38] Alex: We'll redline the NDA if needed.

[00:28:10] Tom: Sounds good. Let's recap next steps quickly.

[00:28:20] Alex: Recap: 1) Alex will send pricing SKUs and contract draft by 04-20. 2) Priya will run bench when MarrowBridge shares sample payloads (Marcus to share S3 link by Monday). 3) Morgan will schedule the weekly cadence starting 04-21. 4) We'll send SOC 2 + K M S integration docs and SSO runbook.
[00:29:00] Marcus: Confirmed.
[00:29:05] Ellen: Confirmed.

[00:29:30] Alex: Anything else — if not, we'll close and follow up with the artifacts. Thanks all.

[00:29:45] (meeting winds down, some crosstalk)
[00:30:10] Priya: I'll follow up with the bench plan template.
[00:30:20] Morgan: I'll send invites and the onboarding checklist.

[00:30:40] End notes:
- Links referenced: V P C checklist (link to internal doc), SOC2 pack (link), Console screenshots (link), bench template (link) — links to be emailed.
- Tone: collaborative, reasonable timeline.

(Transcription noise: occasional word swaps, e.g., "Sock 2" for SOC2, "K V cache" for KV cache, "Redwood Dedic" for Redwood Dedicated.)

End of transcript.
